predecessors.name: Anglo-Saxon England (early settlement)
predecessors.text: the West Saxon core on the south coast of England, which lies inside Cliopatria's single Anglo-Saxon England shape of 441-533 (41 of the 42 cells of Wessex's first shape)

successors.name: Kingdom of England
successors.text: the whole of Wessex's last Cliopatria shape: Wessex, Kent, Sussex, Essex, East Anglia and Mercia, to which Æthelstan added York in 927

rulers.name: Penda of Mercia
rulers.title: King of Mercia, overlord of Wessex

ledger.x: 519: Cerdic becomes the first king of the West Saxons.
577: the West Saxons win at Deorham.
587: the north of the Deorham gains slips away.
628: three cells of the upper Thames pass to Mercia in Cliopatria.
658: Cenwalh takes eastern and central Somerset.
By 685: Centwine takes western Somerset.
686: Cædwalla conquers the South Saxons.
686: Cædwalla conquers the Isle of Wight.
686: Cædwalla installs his brother Mul as king of Kent.
688: Kent is lost.
710: Ine fights Geraint of Dumnonia and advances into Devon.

c. 715: Sussex is independent again. The Kingdom of Sussex infobox: 'Subject to Wessex: c. 686 - c. 715' ('Client state of Wessex (686-715)'); its text: 'Sussex evidently broke away from West Saxon domination some time before 722'. The Ine page has Sussex 'still under West Saxon domination in 710' and Ine invading…
806: three cells of the Thames west of London pass to Mercia in Cliopatria.
825: Egbert reduces Cornwall to a vassal.
825: Egbert beats Beornwulf of Mercia at Ellendun and takes Surrey and Sussex.
825: Kent submits to Wessex.
825: Essex submits to Wessex.
829: Egbert conquers Mercia.
829: the Northumbrians submit at Dore.
830: Wiglaf restores Mercia.
830: the Northumbrian overlordship lapses with Wiglaf's return.
840: Essex leaves West Saxon control for Mercia, on Cliopatria's year only.
876: the Danes seize Wareham.
878: Alfred wins at Edington.
880s: Brycheiniog becomes a vassal of Alfred.
880: Alfred takes over western Mercia when Ceolwulf II is deposed.
886: Alfred retakes London from the Danes.
892: a new Viking army lands in Kent.
896: the Viking army disperses.
911: Æthelred of Mercia dies and Edward takes London and Oxford.
915: Edward takes Bedford.
915: Edward's reconquest of the Danelaw begins in earnest.
917: the Danish armies of Northampton, Cambridge and East Anglia submit.
918: Æthelflaed dies on 12 June and Mercia passes to Edward.
918: Edward rules Mercia directly.
918: the Danelaw south of the Humber is Edward's.
918: the Danish Midlands and East Anglia pass to Wessex.
918: Hywel and Clydog of Seisyllwg submit to Edward.
918: Idwal Foel of Gwynedd gives allegiance to Edward.
926: the border with Gwent is fixed at the Wye.
927: Æthelstan takes York.
927: Wessex becomes the Kingdom of the English.

wars.name: Battle of Deorham
wars.outcome: West Saxon victory: three British kings killed and three cities taken, by the Chronicle's account (the only evidence).

wars.name: Battle of Peonnum
wars.outcome: Cenwalh's West Saxons beat the Britons of Somerset and annex eastern and central Somerset as far as the Parrett, which stayed the border until 681-685.

wars.name: West Saxon advance to the Bristol Channel
wars.outcome: Centwine's victories let the West Saxons occupy western Somerset up to the Bristol Channel.

wars.name: Cædwalla's conquests of Sussex, Kent and the Isle of Wight
wars.outcome: Sussex reduced to subjection and Wight conquered; Kent held only 686-688 under Mul and then lost.

wars.name: Ine's war with Geraint of Dumnonia
wars.outcome: West Saxon advance into Devon; the British win at Hehil in 722 (site unidentified) and the page describes no annexation.

wars.name: Ine's Sussex campaigns
wars.outcome: Ine invaded Sussex in 722 after the exile Ealdbert fled there and again three years later, killing Ealdberht; the page records no territorial result.

wars.name: Battle of Ellandun
wars.outcome: Egbert defeats Beornwulf; Kent, Essex, Surrey and Sussex submit and East Anglia breaks from Mercia.

wars.name: Egbert's conquest of Mercia
wars.outcome: Wiglaf driven into exile in 829 and Mercia held for a year; in 830 he 'obtained the kingdom of Mercia again'.

wars.name: Battle of Hingston Down
wars.outcome: Egbert is beaten by the Danes at Carhampton in 836 and beats the Danes and the West Welsh at Hingston Down in 838, when 'Dumnonian independence may be considered to have ended'.

wars.name: Viking invasion of Wessex
wars.outcome: Alfred buys off the Great Summer Army in 871; Guthrum seizes Wareham in 876 and Exeter, attacks Chippenham in January 878; Alfred wins at Edington and Guthrum is baptised.

wars.name: Alfred's war against the Viking army of 892-896
wars.outcome: The Viking army is held at Farnham and Buttington and blockaded in 894-895; it departs in 896 or 897.

wars.name: Æthelwold's revolt
wars.outcome: Æthelwold seizes Wimborne and Christchurch, goes to Northumbria, returns to Essex in 901 and is killed at the Holme (13 December 902) where the Danes 'kept the place of slaughter'; no border moves.

wars.name: Edward the Elder's reconquest of the Danelaw
wars.outcome: Bedford (915); the Danish armies of Northampton, Cambridge and East Anglia (917); Derby (917) and Leicester (918) to Æthelflaed; Mercia passes to Edward on her death in 918.

wars.name: Æthelstan's conquest of York
wars.outcome: After Sihtric's death Æthelstan invaded and took York; at Eamont on 12 July 927 four kings 'accepted his overlordship'.

certainty.note: No treaty or survey line survives for any frontier: the Thames and Avon boundary against Mercia (Wessex page, 8th century), the Devon-Cornwall frontier and the Welsh march are approximate; Cliopatria's cell shapes are outlines, not lines.

The Alfred-Guthrum treaty ('perhaps in 879 or 880') names a line, 'up the Thames to the Lea, ... to near Luton, ... to Bedford, ... the Ouse to Watling Street', which is sharp; the Welsh, Cornish and Mercian-vassal frontiers stay soft.

The treaty line is gone after Edward's reconquest; the Humber and the York frontier of 927 and the Welsh and Cornish frontiers are approximate (the Tamar boundary of the Æthelstan page rests on William of Malmesbury and is 'treated…
